How to read this atlas

These are source-edition teaching diagrams, not current unit rosters or assigned strength. Solid branches show the documented composition. Dashed branches identify attachments. A person shown inside a child element is already part of that element’s count.

Counting notes
  • Counts are the Required strength column of the TOE s-2025. Positions printed in parentheses are dual designations and are not counted. Officers (O1–O9) and enlisted personnel (EP, E1–E9) are read from the grade rows; civilian employees (SG grades) are shown separately and are not part of personnel totals (the printed aggregate total adds all three).
  • The elements sum to the UMD-counted strength of Headquarters Support Group (161 / 530 / 347; aggregate 1,038): officers 46 + 5 + 90 + 10 + 3 + 7 = 161, EP 199 + 15 + 98 + 32 + 6 + 180 = 530, civilians 143 + 0 + 178 + 18 + 8 + 0 = 347.
  • Discrepancy in the source: the recap of the Headquarters Support Group (page 2) prints 160 / 530 / 347 (aggregate 1,037). The six child files add to 161 officers / 530 EP / 347 civilians (aggregate 1,038) with the Headquarters and Headquarters Service Battalion counted from its manning documents (46 / 199 / 143); at its printed recap (46 / 199 / 142) they add to 161 / 530 / 346. The officer total is therefore 1 above the printed recap either way; by grade the printed recap lists O5 43 and O4 53 where the printed child recaps add to O5 40 and O4 57, and SG11 16 against 15, E6 81 against 80, E4 112 against 113. The tree shows 161 / 530 / 347.
  • Children link to the groups of the separate files, one of each (chart page 1).

Counting notes

Officers (O1–O9) and enlisted personnel (EP, E1–E9) are read from the grade rows; civilian employees (SG grades) are shown separately and are not part of personnel totals (the printed aggregate total adds all three).

Counting notes
  • Counts are the Required strength column of the TOE s-2025. Positions printed in parentheses are dual designations and are not counted. Officers (O1–O9) and enlisted personnel (EP, E1–E9) are read from the grade rows; civilian employees (SG grades) are shown separately and are not part of personnel totals (the printed aggregate total adds all three).
  • The elements sum to the UMD-counted strength of Headquarters and Headquarters Support Group (578 / 1,287 / 772; aggregate 2,637): officers 417 + 161 = 578, EP 757 + 530 = 1,287, civilians 425 + 347 = 772.
  • Mission: To provide administrative, security, and service support function as complementary unit for Headquarters Philippine Army. Basis of allocation: One (1) Headquarters and Headquarters Support Group, Philippine Army. Mobility 85%.
  • Discrepancy in the source: the recap of the Headquarters and Headquarters Support Group (page 4) prints 577 / 1,288 / 772 (aggregate 2,637). The printed recaps of its two children add to 576 / 1,288 / 773 (Headquarters Philippine Army 416 / 758 / 426 + Headquarters Support Group 160 / 530 / 347). With the children counted from their manning documents (Headquarters Philippine Army 417 / 757 / 425, Headquarters Support Group 161 / 530 / 347) the tree adds to 578 / 1,287 / 772 (aggregate 2,637), so the formation recap differs from the children by +1 officer / −1 EP, and the aggregate total agrees. The children’s own discrepancies are described in their groups.
